messages.subject: pcountOpen help
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to use the pcountOpen model on smallmouth bass data from an electrofishing survey that was conducted at 7 sites once a year in June for 8 consecutive years.  When I run the model the SE, z, and P for the detection estimate is "NaN".  Any idea why this is happening?  There is also a warning message - "In sqrt(diag(vcov(obj)) : NaNs produced" 

I have reviewed Dail & Madsen 2010 and the unmarked documentation but can not figure it out.  I tried adjusting the values for "K" and still received the error.  I additionally tried using the negative binomial mixture and values for the estimate of detection with its SE,z and P were returned.  However, the abundance estimates were unreasonably high.  Does this mean the pcountOpen model isn't appropriate to use with my data and the abundance estimates are incorrect?

Thanks for your help!
Jason Doll 

My code is

smb<-matrix(c(4,19,15,13,12,9,3,7,
              15,32,10,23,12,9,3,16,
              41,38,24,27,35,30,21,14,
              21,35,63,29,41,14,26,20,
              25,48,43,24,11,16,7,12,
              10,13,10,18,14,5,8,10,
              81,57,25,23,11,12,23,12),ncol=8)

smbf<-unmarkedFramePCO(y=smb,numPrimary=8)
summary(smbf)

smbmod<-pcountOpen(~1,~1,~1,~1,smbf,mixture="P",K=100)
summary(smbmod)

lamsm<-exp(coef(smbmod,type="lambda"))
gamsm<-exp(coef(smbmod,type="gamma"))
omsm<-plogis(coef(smbmod,type="omega"))
psm<-plogis(coef(smbmod,type="det"))

smb.hat <- matrix(NA, 7, 8)
smb.hat[,1] <- lamsm
for(t in 2:8) {
    smb.hat[,t] <- omsm*smb.hat[,t-1] + gamsm
    }

rbind(N=colSums(smb), smb.hat=colSums(smb.hat))

messages.author: 527e14923215b7e4
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcountOpen help
parts:
Hi Jason,

Thanks for posting the reproducible example. unmarked doesn't try to select smart starting values, so sometimes you need to look at your data and make an educated guess. The log of the counts in year1 is 2.4, so starting at 3 makes sense, and this works:

smbmod1<-pcountOpen(~1,~1,~1,~1,smbf,mixture="P",K=150,
                    starts=c(3,0,0,0))

However, this gives similar results to what you found with the negative binomial model, and so you will probably think that abundance is too high. The reason for the high estimate of abundance is that there is extreme variation in the counts for some sites but not others,

matplot(t(smb), type="b")

and you have no covariates in the model to explain this variation (which may be due to actual abundance or detection). Without covariates, and given the assumed state model, the evidence points to low detection probability. Also, without covariates, your model will probably not pass a goodness-of-fit test.

Richard

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] pcountOpen help
parts:
Richard,

Thanks for the reply and suggestions, I was worried I was way off base.  Providing the starting values you suggested resulted in abundance and detection probability estimates that seam reasonable.  I have a few sites that are close where I have conducted a multi-pass depletion survey of smallmouth bass the past 2 years.  Using the Bayesian probability model for closed populations under unequal catchability described by Mantyniemi et al. (2005) I get first pass detection probabilities between 0.20 and 0.40 compared to 0.27 with the limited sites above.  The depletion sites are only 200m long but if I expand their estimates to 1000m (the distance for the sites above) I get 417 fish/km which is very close to the 351 fish/km estimated for the same year above.

Thanks for the help,
Jason
